description: Random sampler: a jittery clock with two streams of random gates, three clocked random voltages with controllable distribution and quantisation, a slow fourth voltage, and a loop that can lock it all

params.text: Lets the Deja Vu section reach the t generator; with it off that generator makes a fresh random decision every time
Lets the Deja Vu section reach the X generator; with it off that generator makes a fresh random decision every time
Sets the chance that a random decision is taken from the loop instead of made fresh: none at the far counter-clockwise end, a locked loop at noon, and random jumps within the loop past noon
Sets the clock rate, 120 beats per minute at noon; with a cable at the t external clock input it divides or multiplies that clock instead
Sets how the random voltages are spread across the range: a steady voltage at the far counter-clockwise end, a bell curve at noon, flat at two o'clock, and the extremes alone at the far clockwise end
Steps through the seven ways the clock is split between t1 and t3: a complementary coin toss, clusters, drum patterns, independent tosses, a fixed divider, three states, and a Markov generator
Steps through how the three X outputs relate: all three following the panel, the outer two opposing the middle one, or the first opposing the third with the second held in the middle
Sets how many values the loop holds, with 5, 7, 10 and 14 reachable between the printed marks; it is how many values each decision cycles over, not a pattern length in beats
Skews the split between the t1 and t3 outputs; what it changes follows the t mode, from the fairness of the coin toss to the division ratio
Skews the random voltages towards the bottom or the top of the range; it changes which values are likely rather than shifting the values themselves
Steps the clock range between a quarter of the rate, the rate itself, and four times it
Steps the range of the three X outputs between 0V to 2V, 0V to 5V and -5V to 5V
Switches the X generator to sampling the voltage at the X spread input instead of its own random source; X bias then transposes those voltages and X spread sets how far
Sets how far the clock's timing wanders, from perfectly steady to chaos; it applies to an external clock as well as to the internal one
Sets the shape of the random voltages: smooth curves and ramps counter-clockwise of noon, a sample and hold at noon, and quantising past it, with fewer notes of the scale left as it goes
Sets how far the Y output is divided down from the clock of X2, from a sixty-fourth of it to the whole of it
Sets the amplitude of the voltage at the Y output
Skews the voltage at the Y output towards negative or towards positive values
Sets the shape of the voltage at the Y output
Sets the length of the gates at t1 and t3, from 1% to 99% of the interval
Sets how much the length of each gate at t1 and t3 varies at random
Steps through the six scales the X outputs quantise to: major, minor, pentatonic, gamelan, Raag Bhairav That and Raag Shri
Chooses which t outputs clock the X outputs while nothing is patched to the X external clock: each t output to its own X output, or one of the three clocking all of them
Locks the t generator's loop outright, as though the DEJA VU knob were at noon, whatever that knob and the t deja vu button say
Locks the X generator's loop outright, as though the DEJA VU knob were at noon, whatever that knob and the X deja vu button say

inputs.text: Adds to the t BIAS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the X BIAS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
A voltage of 1.7V or more clocks the t generator, taking the place of its internal clock
Adds to the t RATE knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the t JITTER knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the DEJA VU knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the X STEPS knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the X SPREAD knob, 5V covering the whole knob range; with external processing on, or while a scale is being taught, this is the jack the module samples voltages from
A voltage of 1.7V or more clocks all three X outputs, taking the place of whichever t output would otherwise clock them
A rising edge past 1V resets the t generator's counters, dividers and patterns, and reseeds its random source
A rising edge past 1V resets the X generator's counters, dividers and patterns

outputs.text: One of the two streams of random gates derived from the clock, 10V
The clock itself, as 10V pulses, with the jitter applied
The other of the two streams of random gates derived from the clock, 10V
The slow random voltage, -5V to 5V, clocked from a division of the X2 clock
One of the three random voltages, in the range the X range button sets

notes: the module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes a single channel.
the t generator resets itself when the external clock stops: a gap of three seconds, or of four times the last interval between two ticks, whichever is longer, counts as a stop.
a reset of the t generator reaches the X generator as well, unless a cable is patched to the X external clock.
a scale is taught rather than typed: patch a keyboard pitch to the X spread jack and its gate to the X external clock jack, turn Edit current on, play fifty notes or more, then turn it off.
while a scale is being taught, every X output holds the last note played and the gates at the X external clock jack are copied to all three t outputs, so you can hear what you are teaching.
menu: t generator — the submenu holding the t generator's mode, range and reset
Mode: Complementary Bernoulli, Clusters, Drums, Independent Bernoulli, Divider, Three states, Markov — sets how the clock is split between t1 and t3. It is on the t generator submenu
Range: 1/4x, 1x, 4x — sets the clock range. It is on the t generator submenu
Reset/reseed — resets the t generator and gives its random source a new seed. It is on the t generator submenu
X generator — the submenu holding the X generator's mode, range, clock source and reset
Mode: Identical, Bump, Tilt — sets how the three X outputs relate to one another. It is on the X generator submenu
Range: Narrow (0V - 2V), Positive (0V - +5V), Full (-5V - +5V) — sets the range of the X outputs. It is on the X generator submenu
Internal clock source — chooses which t outputs clock the X outputs, and is ignored while a cable is patched to the X external clock. It is on the X generator submenu
Reset — resets the X generator. It is on the X generator submenu
Module seed — the submenu holding the seed the module's random source works from
Reseed rng — gives the random source a new seed chosen by the module. It is on the Module seed submenu
User — takes a seed typed into a text field, from 1 to 4294967295, entered with the return key. It is on the Module seed submenu
Scales — the submenu holding the scale choice, the scale editor and the scale reset
Select active: Major, Minor, Pentatonic, Gamelan (Pelog), Raag Bhairav That, Raag Shri — picks the scale the X outputs quantise to. It is on the Scales submenu
Edit current — turns scale learning on and off; what you play while it is on overwrites the active scale. It is on the Scales submenu
Reset current — puts the factory version of the active scale back. It is on the Scales submenu
